chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Kurdawayh al-Hamdani who said:
I asked the Servant of God (peace be upon him) about the Witr prayer, and he said, 'Connect it.'
For these narrations are not contradictory to what we mentioned, because they included the option (choice) in the Tasleem (saying peace).
And whoever says that it must be connected, then he does not permit the Tasleem in it in any manner.
And if there is choice in it, then we interpret it as referring to the specific Tasleem.
And it is that with us, whoever says 'Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of God' in the Tashahhud, his prayer is broken.
So if he says after that 'Peace be upon you and the mercy of God', it is valid, and if he does not say it, it is also valid.
So the choice only pertained to this type of Tasleem.

And if it were explicit in prohibiting the Tasleem, it would not be obligatory to act upon it, because what we have established regarding the obligation of Tasleem from the narrations is more numerous.
And it is not permissible to deviate from the majority to the minority except for a proof that prevents it.
And it is permissible that these narrations came out via the way of Taqiyya (dissimulation), because they are consistent with the schools of the general public.
And what comes out in this manner is not obligatory to act upon.
And it is probable that he meant by Tasleem that which becomes permissible through Tasleem, such as speech and other things.
And he applied this name to it because it is a cause for its permissibility.
And this speech is something in which a person has a choice: if he wishes, he speaks; and if he wishes, he begins the Witr without speech.
And that which reveals what we mentioned last is what he narrated:

key_terms.التَّسْلِيمِ: Tasleem (saying 'Peace be upon you' to conclude prayer)
key_terms.التَّشَهُّدِ: Tashahhud (the sitting position and recitation in prayer)
key_terms.الْوَتْرِ: Witr prayer (the odd-numbered prayer concluded at night)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on connecting the Witr prayer and the permissibility of Tasleem in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi resolves the apparent contradiction between narrations regarding the Witr prayer by interpreting them as offering a choice between connecting it to the preceding prayers or performing it independently, specifically concerning the validity of the Tasleem. He argues that since the evidence for the obligation of Tasleem is stronger, these narrations are likely based on Taqiyya or refer to the permissibility of speech, thereby preserving the integrity of the prayer. This analysis highlights the Shia scholarly method of reconciling conflicting reports through contextual interpretation and weighing the strength of evidences.
